learning_outcomes.text: Provide an overview of essential subtractive manufacturing processes and their practical applications.
Explain and apply the fundamental principles of various manufacturing processes.
Assess the properties and applications of cutting materials and tools.
Analyze and apply the principles of economic efficiency in manufacturing.
Explain the importance, selection, and use of coolants and lubricants.
Evaluate the machinability of different materials.
Explain and apply the processes of machining with geometrically defined and geometrically undefined cutting edges.
Explain various processes of electro-discharge machining, chemical, and electrochemical material removal and identify their applications.

Understand and apply basic metrological procedures. They can interpret the accuracy specifications of measuring devices and consider them in practice. Furthermore, they are able to evaluate the importance of orders of magnitude and tolerances in the manufacturing process.
Explain the basics of heat treatment and its influence on materials.
Apply theoretical knowledge in practice, prioritize the requirements of affected manufacturing processes, and select suitable manufacturing processes.
Collaborate in a team across disciplines and solve technical tasks jointly.
Reflect on the environmental impacts of various manufacturing processes and promote sustainable methods.
Independently continue their education and recognize and evaluate new developments in the field of manufacturing processes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to various manufacturing processes and their importance in industry
Properties and selection criteria for cutting materials, tool types, and their application areas
Methods for analyzing and increasing the economic efficiency of manufacturing processes
Importance, function, and selection criteria of coolants and lubricants in various manufacturing processes
Influencing factors on machinability and evaluation of machinability of different materials
Principles and techniques of turning, milling, drilling, and other machining processes with geometrically defined cutting edges
In-depth knowledge of grinding, honing, and lapping techniques, as well as machining processes with geometrically undefined cutting edges
Processes of electro-discharge machining, chemical, and electrochemical material removal
Fundamentals of heat treatment and their influence on material properties

Students are able to confidently address questions and requirements of a manufacturing process by competently using common specifications from tool manufacturers, machine tool manufacturers, and coolant suppliers, as well as their catalogs, thereby making informed decisions when selecting suitable solutions and products.
Understanding the interactions between manufacturing processes and other technical, economic, and environmental aspects
Development of skills for independent learning and acquiring new knowledge, as well as adapting to technological innovations and continuous professional development
Exercising appropriate communication skills among themselves, cooperative teamwork, effective task distribution; creating reports and applying documentation skills during internships
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the written examination. A prerequisite for participation in the examination is successful completion of the internship.
